people_spec: Chief Financial Officer (peer independent-school Director of Technology roles report to the CFO)
talk_track: I do technology governance for independent schools — the board-level layer that sits above whatever IT staff and vendors a school already has, without replacing either. CSCS has a live posting for a Director of Technology across all three campuses, and it asks that one person to own infrastructure, networking, cybersecurity, telephone systems, helpdesk operations, budgets and vendors. That combination is worth reading twice: it puts risk decisions and the ticket queue in the same pair of hands, so cybersecurity and vendor accountability get whatever hours are left after the helpdesk. It also means that for however long the search runs, nobody is drafting the answers your board will want if one of your vendors is breached — in the two schools I watched go through the same vendor breach, the one with governance in place recovered in days and the other spent weeks managing parent communication. Worth splitting the governance half from the operations half before you hire? — Kenneth Thomas
notes: Enrollment: CSCS's own 25-26 enrollment table shows 835 total full-time students (725 Colorado Springs, 82 Woodland Park, 28 Lions Online) against an 897 goal — inside Kenneth's 800-2,000 band, and short of goal, which sharpens the enrollment-attrition EDP.
Right side of the market: independent non-denominational nonprofit school, NOT a public district and not an edtech vendor.

Backfill inference (flagged): a LinkedIn profile snapshot dated 2026-05-07 (surfaced via Exa, not visited) lists a current Director of Technology at CSCS since Sep 2023, so the live opening reads as a backfill — i.e. a leadership gap opening now, not a net-new function. Not independently confirmed.

Existing in-house IT staff (systems administrator, computer systems engineer, security coordinator per Exa-surfaced profile snapshots) is a fit, not a conflict: Kenneth sells governance oversight alongside existing staff and vendors rather than replacing them.
Secondary hook: the posting explicitly names 'telephone systems', which maps to his documented ~50% telephony cost cut migrating a 300+ user org off legacy Avaya to Microsoft Teams Phone.
